newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Sinmah in bonus, rights, bonds issues.
newsitem.headline: Sinmah in bonus, rights, bonds issues.

text.p: Malaysian animal feed producer Sinmah Resources Bhd said it would launch bonus and rights issues of new shares, and an issue of bonds with detachable warrants.
Sinmah made the announcement in a statement to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) late on Wednesday.
The proposed bonus issue of five million new shares is on a one-for-four basis, while the rights issue of 15 million new shares is on a three-for-four basis and will be priced at 4.80 ringgit.

Sinmah also said it would issue 50 million ringgit worth of guaranteed redeemable bonds, with an interest rate of 3.50 percent, maturing between 1997 and 2002. These would be issued with 13.33 million detachable warrants.

The proposed rights and bonds issues would raise gross proceeds of 72 million ringgit and 50 million ringgit, respectively, and would be used to pay back bank borrowings and to finance Sinmah's long-term expansion, the company said.

The company's stock had been suspended for the announcement since Tuesday, when it closed at 9.90 ringgit. On Thursday morning, the shares were down 40 cents to 9.50. The shares are listed on the KLSE's Second Board.
The company produces animal livestock feeds and poultry products, and is also involved in property devlopment.
As a result of the proposals, the share capital of the company would be raised from 20 million ringgit to 53.30 million ringgit, the statement said.
